title: Sigmoid
body:
$$
\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}}, \qquad \sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)\left(1 - \sigma(z)\right)
$$

An S-curve squashing all of $\mathbb{R}$ into $(0,1)$: $\sigma(0) = \tfrac12$, and it approaches
$0$ and $1$ without reaching either. The derivative identity is the pleasant part, since the
forward value is already computed and the gradient costs nothing extra.

**Its output reads as a probability**, which is the reason it survives. That is exactly what
[[Logistic Regression]] uses it for, and it is why an [[Output Layer]] doing
[[Binary Classification]] ends in a sigmoid: the number coming out is $P(\text{class }1)$, so
[[Log Loss]] can be computed against it. The multi-class generalisation is softmax, which the vault
has no note for.

## Why it lost the hidden layers to [[ReLU]]

Look at the derivative. $\sigma'$ is largest at $z = 0$, where it equals $\mathbf{0.25}$, and it
falls off toward zero in both directions. Two consequences:

- **It saturates.** For $|z|$ beyond about 5 the curve is flat and the gradient is
  effectively zero, so a unit that gets pushed out there stops learning and there is no force
  pulling it back. This is why [[Weights]] are initialised small.
- **Gradients vanish with depth.** Every layer multiplies the backward signal by at most $0.25$, so
  through $n$ sigmoid layers the gradient shrinks by a factor of at least $4^{-n}$ *even in the
  best case*. Early layers get essentially nothing. [[Chain Rule]] in [[CALCULUS 1]] owns this
  argument; it is the product-of-small-factors picture read pessimistically.

A minor third problem: the output is never negative, so activations are not zero-centred and the
gradients of a layer's weights all share a sign, which makes the descent path zigzag.

$\tanh$ fixes the centring ($\tanh(z) = 2\sigma(2z) - 1$, range $(-1,1)$, derivative up to $1$) but
saturates the same way, so it is a smaller improvement than it looks. [[ReLU]] fixes the vanishing
gradient outright by having derivative exactly $1$ wherever the unit is active.

**The summary worth remembering: sigmoid on the output, [[ReLU]] on the hidden layers.**
